[0] 蘋果近20年其中一場最具代表性活動的問答環節片段已於網上流傳，趁片段未被刪除之前快啲睇。請即觀看以下影片。

[1] 趁蘋果刪片之前快啲睇

[2] Even if you weren't paying close attention to Apple back in 2010, you've likely heard of "Antennagate," and the last-minute press conference Steve Jobs held after being called back from his vacation in Hawaii.

[3] If you're just learning about this now, here's what happened: Shortly after Apple launched the iPhone 4, users discovered that simply holding the phone a different way would cause a noticeable drop in cellular signal.

[4] The fallout was significant enough that Apple had to hastily arrange an event just weeks after the iPhone 4 went on sale.

[5] At the event, Jobs explained that the signal drops weren't unique to the iPhone 4, and offered users a choice: get a free case to prevent their fingers from touching the antenna directly, or return the device for a full refund.

[6] After the event wrapped up, Jobs, along with then-COO Tim Cook and Apple's SVP of Mac Hardware Engineering Bob Mansfield, held a Q&A session with the press.

[7] Since then, there have been numerous accounts of what was said during that Q&A — including one from John Gruber, who recalled asking a question that prompted Jobs, Cook, and Mansfield to each pull a caseless iPhone out of their pockets, producing one of the more memorable photos of the era. But the actual footage of that Q&A had never surfaced. Until now.

[8] Earlier, the YouTube channel Sir Mix-A-Lot Rare Music (which appears to have no connection to the actual Sir Mix-A-Lot) uploaded the full 47-minute Q&A session, which you can watch below:

[9] It's currently unknown how the channel obtained the footage, or whether Apple will issue a copyright takedown request. But now that it's out there, even if the original upload gets removed, copies are likely to pop up elsewhere with ease.

[10] The fact that the video hasn't been taken down yet is itself a good sign. Still, if you want to witness this little piece of Apple history firsthand, it's best to watch it sooner rather than later.

[11] Were you already an Apple fan back during the Antennagate era? Let us know in the comments.
